alignments.note: Consecutive ὥστε rendered by the two-word English introducer *So that*; the complementizer is part of the conjunction's own English realization under rule 40, headed on *So*.

The participle θαρροῦντας is rendered adverbially as *with good courage*. Rule 91's operational test puts the head on *courage*, the word that glosses the θαρρ- lexeme; *with* and *good* are the supplied frame. A head on *with* would rest only on the word standing first, which rule 17 forbids.
Accusative subject of the infinitive, expressed in Greek and written *we* in English, so rule 74's supplied-subject case does not arise.
The infinitive is rendered by the bare finite-looking *say*; the ASV writes no infinitival *to* here, ὥστε having already taken *So that*.

Κύριος is anarthrous, so no article competes and the supplied determiner *The* is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun under rule 51's anarthrous clause. Rule 63 keeps the copula off this subject noun.
Possessive dative ἐμοί rendered by the possessive *my*, as rule 20's possessive-dative case has it; no article stands here for it to displace.
Verbless clause with a noun subject, so rule 63 puts the supplied copula on the predicate nominal rather than on Κύριος: *is … helper*, discontinuous across *my* under rule 15, headed on *helper*.
Ordinary negative aligned to *not*. The variant unit SBLGNT.HEB.13.6.v003 is underdetermined and its fallback remains among the compatible readings, so rule 97 is not in question.
The inflected future takes its English subject and auxiliary under rule 9, headed on the lexical verb *fear*.
Interrogative pronoun τί as the object of ποιήσει, rendered *What*.
Future indicative with its English auxiliary, discontinuous across the inverted subject *man* under rule 15, headed on the lexical verb *do*.
Dative pronoun rendered *unto me*; the case preposition rides with the pronoun under rules 21 and 36.
Anarthrous subject noun, bare *man* in English.
